title: Lighthouse compat litmus: golden prompt corpus and cross-version contract tests for streaming + toolcalls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a resilient, automated litmus suite ("lighthouse") that verifies API compatibility across runtime and SDK versions for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured-output behaviors. The suite will use a curated golden prompt corpus that reflects production surface area (prefetch/kvcache priming, multiplexed streams, interleaved tool calls, partial-JSON emissions, and structured schema migrations). Tests must detect backward-incompatible regressions, flaky interleavings, and silent semantic drift in structured outputs. The output of the suite will feed CI gates, weekly compatibility dashboards, and a small on-call alert set for regressions that exceed predefined thresholds.
steps: Assemble golden prompt corpus: collect ~250 representative prompts from prod telemetry (anonymized) + synthetic edge-cases
Define contract assertions: sequence consistency, tool-call ordering, JSON fragment recovery, schema validation, and KV cache priming visibility
Implement test harness: language-agnostic runner that replays multiplexed stream sessions and records token-level events
Create cross-version matrix: runtime (1.18..1.20), model variants (base/quantized/fallback), SDKs (python/js/go) and region permutations
Instrument CI: integrate into nightly and PR gates with flaky-tolerance and delta-bucket alerts
Add telemetry hooks: fingerprint hashes, per-test latency/cost buckets, and difference visualizations for reviewers
Run initial sweep, triage failures, and land fixes + flaky suppressions with clear root cause notes
acceptance_criteria: Nightly suite completes against runtime-1.18..1.20 without unexpected failures (<=2% flaky failures accepted) for the golden corpus
All contract assertions have machine-readable validators and human-friendly diffs in CI logs
Regression alerting configured: high-severity regressions open tickets automatically and page-on-call when customer_impact is high
Dashboard shows token-level failure classification (protocol, schema, ordering, partial-json) and a searchable history
SDK matrix tests exercise at least one streaming + toolcall interleave per SDK with deterministic seeds for reproducibility
